title: Deer Population
description: A basic population model: births add deer, deaths remove deer.

overview.short: A deer population model with two feedback loops: births drive growth, and deaths limit it.

alt_text: CLD with two loops for deer population: one reinforcing growth and one balancing through deaths.

variables.label: Deer population
variables.description: How many deer there are. It is a stock: it accumulates births and loses deaths.

variables.label: Deer births per year
variables.description: How many deer are born each year. It flows into the population.

variables.label: Deer deaths per year
variables.description: How many deer die each year. It flows out of the population.

loops.name: births loop
loops.narrative: More deer means more births each year, and more births mean even more deer, so the population grows.

loops.name: deaths loop
loops.narrative: More deer means more deaths each year, and more deaths reduce the population, which slows growth.

behavior_graphs.title: Population over time

series.pattern: rises steadily over the whole period
also rises, but stays below births

behavior_graphs.key_insight: Births stay ahead of deaths, so the reinforcing loop dominates and the population keeps growing.

layout_description: The deer population is in the center. Births are on the left with the reinforcing loop, marked R. Deaths are on the right with the balancing loop, marked B.
